title: One-time operations vs repeatable processes

kcs.statement: A one-off task, such as trying out a new service or changing a single setting, fits the Management Console; a task repeated across environments, accounts or Regions should be scripted with the CLI or SDK or defined in templates.
Repeatable, automated processes reduce human error, keep dev, test and production environments identical, and let an environment be rebuilt quickly after a failure.

problem_ideas: An admin must turn on S3 versioning for one bucket, once: console, CLI script or template? Justify the choice.
A team must create the same VPC, subnets and EC2 setup in 12 accounts: which approach, and why is the console a bad choice?
A production outage happened because someone clicked a different setting in prod than in test: name the process change that prevents it.
Sort 8 tasks (rotate one key, nightly report export, new-region rollout, demo for a manager...) into one-time vs repeatable.
A startup rebuilt its environment by hand after a Region issue and took 3 days: what would a repeatable process have changed?
Distractor drill: 'the fastest way to deploy identical environments repeatedly' with options console, CLI one-liner, template, support ticket.
